business_summary: Mahindra & Mahindra is an Indian automobiles company. Revenue has grown 17.85% a year over three years to FY26. FY26 operating margin was 18.62% and net profit was Rs 17,098.85 crore, with no loss-making quarter in the last four. Debt/equity is 1.47x.
why_own: The case rests on sustained double-digit revenue growth, with a 3-year revenue CAGR of 17.85% and net profit CAGR of 18.48%, plus a 3-year operating margin gain of 1.87 pp and ROE of 20.1%. Trailing P/E of 19.32x is 8.85% below its own 5-year median, but cash flow is only 0.68x of profit and leverage is 1.47x. No investor documents were supplied, so the drivers are metric-only.

drivers.statement: Revenue keeps compounding at a double-digit rate; the 3-year revenue CAGR is currently 17.85%. (warn line tightened by code from 12 to 12.5.)
Operating margin holds near the current 18.62%, which is up 1.87 pp over three years.
Returns on capital stay healthy; ROCE is currently 15.12% and ROE is 20.1%.
Leverage stays contained; debt/equity is currently 1.47x and interest cover is 3.63x.

kill_criteria.description: ROCE falls below 10%, so returns on capital are no longer healthy.
Interest cover falls below 2x, leaving little room for debt service.
Operating margin falls below 13%, undoing the margin gains of the last three years.

risks.statement: Cash conversion is weak: FY26 cash from operations was only 0.68x of net profit. The cause is not tested here.
Borrowings are meaningful at 1.47x equity, and interest cover is 3.63x. A profit downturn would squeeze debt service.
Valuation is not cheap on book value at 3.83x price/book and 19.32x trailing P/E. A fall in growth or margins could compress the multiple even though P/E is 8.85% below its own 5-year median.

skeptic_counter_case: The thesis is wrong if growth keeps slowing and leverage stops being benign. Growth is already decelerating (5y CAGR 21.74% vs 3y 17.85%). ROE of 20.1% sits well above ROCE of 15.12%, and cash from operations is only 0.68x of profit. Interest cover is 3.63x. The thresholds are lenient: K3 trips only after margin falls 5.62 pp, three times the 1.87 pp gain it claims to protect. D1 breaks only if growth falls by more than half. P/E is just 8.85% under its median, so the multiple gives little cushion. What would change this view: Operating cash flow recovering to roughly 1x of net profit while 3-year revenue CAGR stays above the 12.5% warn line would remove most of my objection.
